summary.text: Jane Beaulieu is the Democratic candidate for the New Hampshire House of Representatives, Hillsborough 19, in the November 3, 2026 general election.

She is a former state representative and former Manchester school board member who, according to Ballotpedia, served in the House from 2004 to 2010 and from 2012 to 2024, and she did not file for re-election in 2024.

paragraphs.text: Beaulieu was born in Manchester, graduated from Manchester Memorial High School and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of New Hampshire, according to Ballotpedia.

Ballotpedia also lists a certificate from the Nackey Loeb School of Communications and a professional background as a licensed cosmetologist, owner of Janet Beanstalk/Cafe/Florist, educator and administrator.
Beaulieu was first elected to the New Hampshire House from Hillsborough 17, where Ballotpedia lists her in office from 2004 to 2010.
She returned in 2012 representing Hillsborough 45, won re-election in 2018 and 2020 alongside Connie Van Houten, and was re-elected in 2022 from the redistricted Hillsborough 19 seat.
In 2019 she was elected to the Manchester Board of School Committee, Ward 10, defeating incumbent John B. Avard, and Ballotpedia lists her in that office from 2020 to 2022.
Her House committee assignments included Environment and Agriculture in 2019-2020, Commerce and Consumer Affairs in 2021-2022, and Commerce and Consumer Affairs as clerk in 2023-2024.
She advanced from the Democratic primary on September 8, 2026, alongside Chrissy Simonds.
